text:
Anya: Quick follow-up to the handshake RFC — I reviewed the shim and think we need to tighten the minimal surface between hosted / dedicated / private. Two immediate concerns: auth token shapes and telemetry sampling. Thoughts?

Mike: +1. Biggest ops risk is private customers demanding strict token lifetimes. We should avoid forcing short-lived KMS-attested tokens on the hosted fallback path; that makes fallbacks brittle.

Jess: Agreed. My rough take: define two auth tiers — opaque-bearer for hosted and signed-JWT (with kid claim) for dedicated/private. Adapters should accept both and normalize into an internal session object with fields tenant_id, auth_tier, origin. Keeping it small: mapping table + verifier per tier. See internal note: <https://redwood.internal/rfc/handshake#auth>

Rik: Normalization is fine but don't lose routing/obs context. If we flatten origin away we lose the ability to debug cross-mode fallbacks. Suggest we keep a low-cardinality 'flavor' tag (hosted/dedicated/private) that gets propagated to traces/metrics only.

Anya: Good call. Proposal: add header X-RW-Flavor (values: hosted|dedicated|private) for telemetry, and a separate security_profile metadata (values: lax|standard|strict) for auth strength. That prevents cardinality explosion while keeping both concerns separate.

ops-bot: deploy/job 71234 completed on infra-stage — tagging this thread for visibility. :rocket:

Jess: I'll prototype a lightweight adapter that accepts both token shapes and emits the normalized session. Prototype will include a tiny mapping table and unit tests. Rough mapping example:

```
# pseudo mapping (adapter)
if token.type == "opaque":
  session.auth_tier = "opaque"
  session.security_profile = "lax"
else if token.type == "jwt":
  session.auth_tier = "jwt"
  session.security_profile = "standard"
```

ETA: EOD for a first pass.

Mike: On fallback semantics — we cannot silently change model variants or capability in-hosting mode. If hosted routes to dedicated, the response must include a degrade signal header (X-RW-Degraded: reason) and a metric with tag fallback=dedicated. Tenants must be able to opt out of transparent fallbacks.

Rik: +1. Also caching corner: prefix/KV TTLs must be namespaced by host-mode. If we reuse caches across modes when routing flips, we risk leaking private prefixes into hosted artifacts. Explicit namespace prevents that.

Anya: Action items: 1) Jess — prototype adapter + PR, 2) Rik — spec for low-cardinality telemetry header + cache namespacing, 3) Mike — write fallback signalling and opt-out policy, 4) Anya — update RFC with auth tiers and header names. Meeting if needed Thurs 10am to align. :calendar:

Jess: Noted. Creating PR and will drop link here once ready.

Mike: Sounds good. Will review the PR and add fallback policy draft. :thumbsup:

Anya: Thanks all — let's avoid large surface changes in the shim; prefer small, explicit knobs that keep cross-mode behavior observable and revertible.
